<p className="kicker">Every graft command, grouped by when you use it.</p>

Look up a command here. In a terminal, `graft --help` lists the commands and
`graft <command> --help` shows one command's usage and flags. To read graft's
output from a script or an agent, see [Script the CLI](/docs/cli).

This page is generated from the table the CLI's own help reads, so the two
always match. `graft migrate` and `graft merge` only report what they would
change until you pass `--apply`.

## Set up a project

### `graft create`

Make a new site: a template, a database, Studio and (by default) a Next.js app, installed and ready. `npm create graft` runs this. It asks a few questions; flags answer them, and --yes takes the defaults for the rest.

```text
graft create [dir] [--template <name>] [--edit online|code] [--database new|none|<url>] [--framework next|none] [--yes] [--no-install] [--no-input]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--template <name>` | blog, docs, shop, portfolio or blank (default: blog). |
| `--edit online\|code` | online keeps content in the database, edited in Studio (default); code keeps it as files in git. |
| `--database new\|none\|<url>` | new makes a free Postgres to claim later; none compiles content to a file (with --edit code); or your own Postgres 13+ URL. |
| `--framework next\|none` | next for a Next.js site that shows every collection (default); none for only the content. |
| `-y, --yes` | Use the default for every question a flag did not answer. |
| `--no-install` | Write the files and stop before installing. |
| `--no-input` | Never stop to ask a question. Same as `GRAFT_PROMPT_DISABLED`. |

Needs no database. May ask questions on a terminal; `--no-input` never does.

```sh
graft create my-site --template docs --edit code --database none --yes
```

### `graft init`

Scaffold a Graft project in dir (default: here). The static engine is the default: no database and no environment variables.

```text
graft init [dir] [--static] [--postgres] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--static` | Static engine: no database, no env (the default). |
| `--postgres` | Postgres engine: operational data, typed functions, database branching. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft doctor`

Check this project's setup: the database, its schema, content, the index and Studio sign-in. Prints a checklist and the one thing to do next.

```text
graft doctor [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Uses `DATABASE_URL` when it is set, and works without it. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

| Exit code | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Everything is set up. |
| `1` | Something is missing; the output says what to do next. |

### `graft add`

Copy an owned primitive (and the primitives it needs) from the registry into graft/, and regenerate the graft/ barrel. graft.config.ts needs no edit. With no item, list the primitives you can add.

```text
graft add [item...] [--dry-run] [--overwrite] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without changing it. |
| `--overwrite` | Replace files that differ from the registry's. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

```sh
graft add comments --dry-run
```

## Write and check content

### `graft compile`

Check every content file and build the index, once.

```text
graft compile [--branch <id>] [--prune-unknown] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--prune-unknown` | Remove index entries in collections the schema no longer has (default: refuse, which protects a shared DATABASE_URL). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL` on the Postgres engine; none on the static engine. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

```sh
graft compile --json > changes.json
```

### `graft dev`

Watch content/ and graft.config.ts, and compile on every change.

```text
graft dev [--branch <id>]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |

Needs `DATABASE_URL` on the Postgres engine; none on the static engine. Runs until you stop it.

### `graft check`

Check every content file the way a compile or a publish would: the schema, slug uniqueness, MDX safety, and references to documents that don't exist. Needs no database.

```text
graft check [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

| Exit code | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `1` | At least one file has a problem; each is listed. |

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

List recent compiles and what each one changed.

```text

```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |

### `graft asset put`

Upload a binary to the asset store (S3_* env) and print the frontmatter reference. The key defaults to assets/\<file name>. A key that already holds a file is refused with ASSET_EXISTS, because the store keeps no version history.

```text
graft asset put <file> [key] [--overwrite] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--overwrite` | Replace the file already stored under the key. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

```sh
graft asset put ./hero.png assets/hero.png
```

## Run Graft

### `graft mcp`

Serve the project MCP over stdio: content and function tools, for .mcp.json and other local agents. On the Postgres engine it needs DATABASE_URL.

```text
graft mcp [--branch <id>] [--elicit-approvals]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--elicit-approvals` | Ask this terminal's operator to decide a destructive call, instead of failing with an id for graft approve. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL` on the Postgres engine; none on the static engine.

### `graft serve`

Run the headless Graft runtime over HTTP: POST /api/fn/\<name>, POST /api/mcp, GET /api/content/v1/*, GET /healthz. This is what a self-hosted container runs.

```text
graft serve [--branch <id>] [--port <n>] [--host <host>] [--studio]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--port <n>` | Port to listen on (default: 3903). Same as `PORT`. |
| `--host <host>` | Host to listen on (default: 127.0.0.1, this computer only). Same as `HOST`. |
| `--studio` | Serve Studio at /studio too. Same as `GRAFT_STUDIO`. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Runs until you stop it.

### `graft studio`

Run Studio: edit content, approve or deny actions, and read the OpenAPI document. Without a database, saves go to your files.

```text
graft studio [--branch <id>] [--port <n>] [--host <host>]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--port <n>` | Port to listen on (default: 4983). Same as `GRAFT_STUDIO_PORT`. |
| `--host <host>` | Host to listen on (default: 127.0.0.1, this computer only). Same as `HOST`. |

Uses `DATABASE_URL` when it is set, and works without it. Runs until you stop it.

### `graft studio invite`

Print a sign-in link for someone without a GitHub account. It is signed with GRAFT_STUDIO_SECRET and expires after --days. To give someone an account instead, invite them from Studio's Settings.

```text
graft studio invite <email> [--role <role>] [--name <name>] [--days <n>] [--url <url>] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--role <role>` | viewer, contributor, editor (default) or admin. |
| `--name <name>` | The name commits are attributed to. |
| `--days <n>` | How long the link works, 1 to 30 (default: 7). |
| `--url <url>` | Where Studio is served. Same as `GRAFT_STUDIO_URL`. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft studio setup-code`

Print the code a hosted Studio asks for before it creates the owner account. It comes from GRAFT_STUDIO_SECRET, so run it with the site's settings.

```text
graft studio setup-code
```

Needs no database.

## Keep content in the database

### `graft content import`

For a project with content = \{ source: "database" }: load the files under the content directory into the database. Every file is checked first. Only documents with nothing published come in: a published document is never overwritten, and a missing file deletes nothing. To change published content, use Studio or graft push.

```text
graft content import [--branch <id>] [--dry-run] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without changing it. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft pull`

For a project with content = \{ source: "database" }: write what is published into the files under the content directory. A file you changed since your last pull is kept for graft push. One changed both here and in the database is left as it is and listed, unless --force takes the published version.

```text
graft pull [doc...] [--branch <id>] [--only <doc>]... [--force] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--only <doc>` | Only this document, like posts/launch (same as naming it as an argument). Repeat it for more than one. |
| `--force` | Settle a conflict: pull takes the published version, push publishes yours. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

```sh
graft pull posts/launch
```

### `graft push`

Publish the files you changed since your last graft pull, checked as graft compile checks them. Refused, with nothing written, if someone published one of those documents since your pull: pull first. --force publishes over it.

```text
graft push [doc...] [--branch <id>] [--only <doc>]... [--dry-run] [--force] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--only <doc>` | Only this document, like posts/launch (same as naming it as an argument). Repeat it for more than one. |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without changing it. |
| `--force` | Settle a conflict: pull takes the published version, push publishes yours. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft mirror`

Commit everything published since the last run to the GitHub repository in GRAFT_GITHUB_REPO, as one commit. Run it on a schedule, or let graft serve do it when graft.config.ts sets content.mirror.

```text
graft mirror [--branch <id>] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

## Manage the database

### `graft db migrate`

Apply the Postgres schema migrations that ship with @usegraft/db. This is the first command a Postgres-engine project runs.

```text
graft db migrate [--dry-run] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | List pending schema migrations without applying them. |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft db claim`

Keep the free database `graft create --database new` made. Prints the link to claim it (a free Neon account), waits until you have, then asks for the new connection string and saves it to .env. Claiming changes the password, so the old DATABASE_URL stops working.

```text
graft db claim [--url <postgres-url>] [--no-input]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--url <postgres-url>` | The claimed database's connection string, instead of the question. |
| `--no-input` | Never stop to ask a question. Same as `GRAFT_PROMPT_DISABLED`. |

Needs no database. May ask questions on a terminal; `--no-input` never does.

### `graft migrate`

Show pending content and data migrations. --apply runs them and records each in the ledger. A concurrent --apply on the same branch waits for this one and then skips what it applied.

```text
graft migrate [--branch <id>] [--apply] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `-b, --branch <id>` | Content branch to work on (default: main). |
| `--apply` | Make the change (without it, only report what would change). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft harden`

Grant an existing Postgres role the runtime privilege set: it can request and consume approvals but never decide them.

```text
graft harden <role> [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

## Work with preview branches

### `graft branch`

List branches.

```text

```

Create a preview branch.

### `graft branch drop`

Delete a branch: purge an overlay's rows, or delete a Neon fork.

```text

```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft merge`

Merge a branch: replay its migrations, move its data, recompile.

```text

```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--into <target>` | Branch to merge into (default: main). |
| `--apply` | Make the change (without it, only report what would change). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs `DATABASE_URL`. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

## Keep CI cheap

### `graft ci changes`

Print content-only=true when every changed file is content, and write it to $GITHUB_OUTPUT for later steps to read.

```text
graft ci changes [--base <ref>] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--base <ref>` | Git ref to compare against (default: the pull request's base, the host's previous deploy, or the commit a push started from). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

### `graft ci skip-build`

Exit 0 when the deploy can be skipped: only content changed, and the site already serves it from the database. Never skips on the previous commit alone.

```text
graft ci skip-build [--base <ref>] [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--base <ref>` | Git ref to compare against (default: the pull request's base, the host's previous deploy, or the commit a push started from). |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

| Exit code | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Skip the build. |
| `1` | Build. |

### `graft ci init`

Write a workflow that runs graft check on content changes.

```text
graft ci init [--overwrite]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--overwrite` | Replace the workflow file if it exists. |

Needs no database.

## Learn the CLI

### `graft help`

Show help for a command or a topic.

```text
graft help [command-or-topic...]
```

Needs no database.

```sh
graft help branch create
graft help exit-codes
```

### `graft commands`

List every command; --json describes each one and its flags.

```text
graft commands [--json]
```

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print one JSON object on stdout; messages go to stderr. |

Needs no database. Prints its answer as JSON with `--json`.

## Exit codes

Every command exits with one of these, unless its entry above lists its own.

| Exit code | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | It worked. |
| `1` | It failed; the error says why and what to do. |
| `2` | The command was called wrong: an unknown command or flag, or a missing argument. Nothing ran. |
| `3` | A person has to approve the action first. Run `graft approve <id>`, then repeat it. |
| `4` | The credential is missing, wrong, or lacks the access this needs. |

## Environment variables

These change how the CLI behaves. Your project's own settings are on the
[Configuration](/docs/configuration) page.

| Variable | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | The Postgres database. Read from the environment, or from `.env` in this folder or any folder above it. |
| `GRAFT_DEBUG` | Set to 1 to print the stack trace of an unexpected error. |
| `GRAFT_PROMPT_DISABLED` | Set to 1 to never ask a question, as `--no-input` does. |
| `GRAFT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` | Set to 1 to never check npm for a newer Graft. Also read from `.env`. |
| `CI` | When set, the update check is off. |
| `NO_COLOR` | When set, never print color. |
| `FORCE_COLOR` | When set, print color even when the output is not a terminal. |
| `CLICOLOR` | Set to 0 to turn color off on a terminal. |
| `CLICOLOR_FORCE` | Same as `FORCE_COLOR`. |
| `TERM` | `dumb` turns color off. |
| `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | Where the update check caches its answer, under `graft/` (default: `~/.cache`). |
| `npm_config_registry` | The npm registry the update check asks. |

## Which commands need a database

Graft reads `.env` from the current folder or any folder above it.

- **Always need `DATABASE_URL`:** `graft content`, `graft compilations`, `graft serve`, `graft content import`, `graft pull`, `graft push`, `graft mirror`, `graft db migrate`, `graft migrate`, `graft harden`, `graft approvals`, `graft approve`, `graft deny`, `graft branch`, `graft branch create`, `graft branch drop`, `graft merge`.
- **Need it on the Postgres engine only:** `graft compile`, `graft dev`, `graft mcp`.
- **Use it when it is set:** `graft doctor`, `graft studio`.
- **Never need it:** `graft create`, `graft init`, `graft add`, `graft check`, `graft asset put`, `graft studio invite`, `graft studio setup-code`, `graft db claim`, `graft ci changes`, `graft ci skip-build`, `graft ci init`, `graft help`, `graft commands`.
